title: Support-Aware Identification with Functional Variables and Declared Structural Zeros
banked_reason: The latent FID-S trichotomy promised by the proposal is not delivered: its grammar, independent-source lift, rational witnesses, converse reconstruction, certificate syntax, kill audit, and global bounds remain open.
gap_reasons: The latent FID-S trichotomy promised by the proposal is not delivered: this node expressly leaves the grammar, latent independent-source lift, rational witnesses, formula reconstruction, and global bounds open, while the proved kernel is restricted to the fully observed case and an abstract conditional ID embedding.

The headline algorithmic-identification deliverable has no executable production system, terminal-certificate syntax, or computable formula/witness output; construction handles and an open-ended question cannot supply the required support-valid FID-S map.
proof_attempt_summary: The run corrected the comparator literature, verified eight cited lemmas from official sources, and proved a finite support oracle, a tunable fully observed completion frontier, a supported-bow separating pair, and an abstract classical-ID compiler theorem. It did not construct the advertised latent FID-S grammar or prove the independent-source latent lift, rational equal-law witness theorem, converse formula reconstruction, certificate syntax, kill-instance audit, or global bounds. The D0.5 panel and an independent validity gate therefore classified the claimed latent kernel as substituted rather than merely incomplete at a lower novelty tier.
tldr: This note formulates, but does not construct, a bounded support-aware grammar for FID-S. The intended procedure concerns finite latent DAGs with supplied observed alphabets, qualitative functional nodes, and declared positive or zero observed events, and would return an inconsistency certificate, a guarded identifying formula, or an exact-support rational separating pair. The proved classical result is conditional and abstract: any restricted grammar instance satisfying the local seven-case interface reproduces ordinary ID; no such concrete FID-S grammar instance is constructed here. The fully observed completion frontier is proved: for each obstruction and each integer \(r\geq 3\), an existentially selected common-law fiber has target gap at least \(1-2/r\), primitive denominator at most \(r|V|\max_{i\in V}|\Omega_i|\), and the stated logarithmic primitive-bit bound. The case \(r=8\) gives the \(3/4\)-gap corollary, but no constant-gap claim is made for every fixed observational law on the same support. The dedicated proposition proves the bow example \(\mathcal B_0\) directly, making it a mandatory regression test for any future trichotomy. The general support-preserving independent-source latent lift, rational equal-law witness theorem, converse formula reconstruction, concrete finite grammar, certificate syntax, and global search bounds remain open.
gap: Ordinary hedge completeness ignores declared structural-zero faces. Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under stated separability and parent conditions, and Theorem 18 assumes the treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); neither theorem identifies the arbitrary declared zero-and-positive support-literal regime introduced here. Chen--Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2 are sound formula-returning algorithms for state-based effects under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints with a strictly positive observational law, not a complete formula-or-exact-support-countermodel procedure for valid intervention states on structural-zero faces. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash prove sound-and-complete gID under positivity of the observational law, not on arbitrary declared support faces, and do not supply exact-support rational paired witnesses. Tikka--Hyttinen--Karvanen Theorem 5 supplies a terminating sound CSI search, and Theorem 6 shows why contextwise answers do not give completeness.
fill: A terminating \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\) procedure will preserve \(\Omega\), support, functional-row provenance, and the latent-source architecture of \(G\) through recursion and certify every terminal outcome with a guarded formula, a contradiction, or a rational separating pair obeying explicit primitive and total bit bounds. The grammar construction must also provide finite certificate syntax, decidable rule checking, and explicit checker and search complexity bounds.
